item.title: capture: public first-post edit form and answers (LOT-048 inputs)
item.body:
Refs #265
Claim: mac/cap-public-writes-opus

Not a lot: capture batch for LOT-048 (#74) and LOT-036 (#63), part B of the operator-approved public-write capture (part A: #258). What is left on #265: the delete answer of a public first post (not authorised, stays pending capture).

**Problem.** The public first-post edit form (subject field, delete label) could only come from a topic an operator account started. Its topic id, message ids, subject, text and dates would tie `user1` to the real account (anyone can open the topic and read its author).

**What changed.**
- Anonymizer: new `own_topics` key in the git-ignored local config. On a page of such a topic it replaces:
  - the topic id with `9900001`;
  - the message ids with `9910000001`…, using one table per publish batch;
  - the subject and slug;
  - message bodies, the form review and the description;
  - each line of the edit text, keeping the line breaks;
  - form-encoded request bodies;
  - the "Sujets relatifs" links;
  - every date, and the meta date.

  An independent verifier (`verify_own_topic`, its own patterns) reports any of these positions left real on a page or meta naming a fake own topic id. It runs in `check --corpus`. `check --config` is mandatory for such a batch, as documented in the kit README and FIXTURES.md.
- Corpus: `R63a`, `R63e` (the topic page before and after), `R63b` (first-post edit form: action `/bdd.php`, visible `sujet` maxlength 70, `subcat` select, poll fields, "Effacer l'intégralité du sujet"), `W34` (edit answer), `W35` (restore answer: the stored text and subject were then byte-identical to the original). Also MANIFEST rows; R63c and R63d are captured but not published (verification reads only).
- LOT-004 oracles for R63b (form, edit), W34 and W35 (response).
- HFR-PROTOCOL §3.1 and the LOT-036 edit-form rows now cover the public first post. In LOT-036 and LOT-048 the pending first-post edit form is settled. The engine still asks for whole-topic confirmation on public deletes; trusting the signs on public forms is a separate decision.

**Anonymization.** `check --corpus` 240/240 and `check --config` clean. Independent checks over the raw files found no leak:
- one check covers names, tokens, cookies and ids;
- an own-topic check covers the topic and message ids, dates, times, subject and slug, and words of the sale text and replies.

Corpus reviewed by Fable: APPROVE, and its three low findings are fixed (unquoted JS ids, documented `check --config`, R63c/R63d recorded).

**Tests.**
- `tooling/fixtures/tests/test_own_topic.py`: one test per position. Each checks that the verifier reports the raw value and that the anonymizer replaces it; removing a rule fails its test.
- `HopFormOracleTests` with R63b, `HopResponseParserTests` with W34 and W35 (differential tests and the corpus sweep), and `PostingBodyOracleTests` with R63b.
- Kit tests and `swift test` are green.

This change extends fixture anonymization and verification for operator-owned public topics and adds first-post edit and restore captures with parser and posting test coverage. It affects only test and tooling artifacts, so production behavior is unchanged. No concrete merge-blocking issue remains after review.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to 7e7d0
The change improves protection of operator identity in published captures. Exposure remains limited to an operator-run publication workflow, and no actual disclosure was established. One uncertainty remains: the anonymizer and its checker can both miss identifying text in a particular title-cell layout whose use by supported captures is unconfirmed. **Retained concerns** - **Medium · security · inferred:** The new excerpt rewriter and verifier share a text-boundary assumption: arbitrary text immediately after the closing title anchor can escape both. Whether supported captures produce that layout remains unresolved, so this is a privacy-assurance concern rather than a confirmed disclosure.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The relevant exposure is operator identity and linkability through published capture pages and metadata. It is bounded by the topics and captures selected for publication; the inspected change does not grant additional forum privileges. Exploitation of the deferred layout case would still require affected content to enter the operator-run publication workflow. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _inferred_ — The deferred path is capture content containing identifying raw text immediately after the title anchor, followed by anonymization and verification that both miss that leading text, then publication. Other rules may remove recognized names or identifiers, but do not establish removal of arbitrary identifying prose. Existing excerpt examples contain nested markup and provide counterevidence to current exposure, not proof that the disputed layout is supported. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The raw-to-publishable boundary combines configured ownership, redaction, and pre-write checks. Remaining configured real topic identifiers are reported directly; the owned-topic verifier activates on fake-topic markers. Consequently, the documented configuration-aware check remains necessary alongside configuration-free corpus checking. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Page and metadata writes are separate rather than transactional, but that behavior predates this PR. All five newly listed captures use HTML and therefore take the page-first alias initialization path; the metadata-only limitation does not establish a newly introduced exposure for these entries. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Make excerpt validation cover leading and trailing text independently of the rewriter's tag-boundary assumptions. Resolve the remaining reachability question using authentic supported capture layouts before treating owned-topic privacy coverage as complete.
